Team description

SumUp's Hardware Development team builds the physical products millions of small businesses rely on every day, and this role sits right at the start of a new chapter: moving our in-house hardware onto the Android platform for the first time. This isn't a typical Android device, it's a highly customised, security-first product built from scratch, which means the person joining will help define how the operating system, drivers, and secure processor come together rather than inheriting someone else's setup. The team works closely with hardware, software, and QA engineers across the bring-up process, so this role offers a rare chance to shape a product's foundations while working alongside experienced embedded and secure processor leads.

What you'll do

  • Support system bring-up for the new Android embedded platform, from bootloader through to kernel and framework
  • Integrate and maintain kernel modules and drivers, including power management and connectivity components
  • Contribute to build system integration across the platform
  • Debug hardware and software issues at the protocol level and help resolve critical issues found during testing
  • Carry out testing and validation to confirm the platform is stable and secure before release

You'll be great for this role if…

  • Experience developing embedded systems with a strong focus on Android OS, gained over several years in a professional setting
  • Strong knowledge of the Android OS architecture, from bootloader (U-Boot, Little Kernel) and kernel through to framework and services
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware interfaces at protocol level, including I2C, SPI, UART, and SDIO
  • Solid understanding of embedded security concepts such as Secure Boot, TrustZone (TEE), dm-verity, encryption, and hardware-backed key storage
  • Comfort working with Qualcomm Snapdragon or MediaTek platforms, and expert-level C programming for embedded Linux environments

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with SumUppers globally on large-scale fintech products used by millions of businesses worldwide, from our Berlin office. This involves an office-first setup 

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

💶 A corporate pension scheme where we match up to 20% of your contributions

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

data.title: Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, DashOS EMEA
data.description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

DashOS is DoorDash's merchant technology platform. It brings together the products restaurants and local businesses use to run their own business, sell on their own channels and keep their guests coming back, including online ordering, websites and apps, and loyalty. DashOS connects these tools with the demand and growth learnings of the DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo marketplaces, so merchants can grow both on our marketplaces and on their own channels.

In EMEA, we are building DashOS market by market. The team is small and works like a startup within the larger DoorDash. When joining DashOS, you will help shape a new business from an early stage: what we offer merchants to fuel their growth, how we take it to market and how we support merchants once they are live.

Our Strategy & Operations team builds the DashOS business end to end in EMEA: what we focus on, how we measure success, and the playbooks that make growth repeatable. We work in small cross-functional pods that find improvement opportunities, launch and iterate, together with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Legal, Marketing, our merchant and consumer teams.

About the Role

We are now looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Operations to build the commercial engine behind DashOS. You will own the systems, numbers and operating rhythm that turn a multi-product strategy into predictable revenue, across all DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo markets in EMEA.

What you'll be doing

As the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations for DashOS EMEA, you will partner directly with DashOS commercial leadership to co-own the go-to-market plan and run the operating cadence for the sales and account management teams selling DashOS. This is a senior individual contributor role for a builder: you will set up the tracking and planning foundations, then use them to make the sales organisation measurably better.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Build the revenue tracking infrastructure: own our CRM setup and the data flows into our BI stack, so pipeline, activities and revenue for every DashOS product live in one place
  • Run the commercial operating cadence, including pipeline tracking, pacing and weekly forecasting with sales and account managers, and own the DashOS commercial narrative to EMEA leadership
  • Own sales planning across markets: set targets and quotas through bottom-up and top-down allocation, and design books of business, territories and coverage models that match our growth goals
  • Turn sales performance data into action by building dashboards that act as the single source of truth for account-level performance and risk, and surfacing insights that managers and sellers can act on
  • Design and roll out incentive systems, including MBOs, SPIFFs and variable compensation, together with Finance, so sales and account managers own DashOS revenue alongside marketplace revenue
  • Make DashOS part of the core commercial motion, so it shows up in every account manager's book of business, account plans and business reviews rather than running on the side
  • Automate and scale with AI, removing manual work for sellers and managers (e.g. pre-populated account plans, automated pipeline views) so teams spend their time with merchants

Our humble expectations

  • Significant experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy & Operations or a similar commercial role, ideally in a fast-growing tech company. A management consulting background is a plus.
  • A track record in sales planning: quota and target setting, territory and book-of-business design, and forecasting cadences for a multi-market sales organisation.
  • Hands-on with data and systems. You are comfortable with SQL and BI tools (e.g. Looker, Tableau) and have worked deeply in a CRM such as Salesforce. You build things yourself rather than only writing specs.
  • Experience designing incentive models, variable pay structures, SPIFFs and performance tracking across commercial teams.
  • A builder and generalist who is comfortable with ambiguity, can take a broad mandate and turn it into concrete outputs, and doesn't need a fully built stack to deliver.
  • A clear communicator and trusted partner to senior leaders, able to translate data into a commercial narrative and build alignment across Sales, Finance and Product.
  • Strong understanding of distinct sales motions, including Enterprise Sales, SMB Sales and Account Management. Experience with multi-product or platform sales is a plus.
  • Bonus: experience using AI and automation to scale commercial operations.

Why join us

You will do work that matters and help build one of DoorDash's next big bets. Working here, you can expect to:

  • Make a visible impact every day, directly improving how merchants run and grow their business.
  • Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment, with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.
  • Build a career, not just a role, as DashOS grows across EMEA.
  • Deliver together in an inclusive, diverse and values-driven culture, with big hearts and small egos.

Next steps

If you are excited about building a new business from an early stage and taking real ownership, click below to apply, add your CV and get the conversation going! We review applications on an ongoing basis. 💙

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

data.title: Account Development Representative I - DACH
data.description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a German-speaking ADR I to join our Account Development team at Camunda.

 

We're a tight-knit, energetic team that takes outbound seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We run structured prospecting motions, share what's working in real time, celebrate the wins together, and still allow for flexibility in the way we operate because booking a good meeting takes real work and progressing an opportunity puts ADRs at the forefront of a great GTM motion.

 

This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time.

What you will do:

As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion.

  • Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts.

  • Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives.

  • Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions.

  • Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback.

  • Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance.

  • Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in German

  • Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Internships, retail, hospitality, or customer support all count if you know how to build rapport with people, manage expectations and handle rejection.

  • Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads.

  • Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You don't need an engineering background, but you need to be genuinely interested in understanding what Camunda does and why it matters to the people you're calling. You share successes.

  • Resilience and self-awareness. You know how to keep going without getting discouraged, and you can tell the difference between a bad day and a bad approach.

  • Coachability. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it.

  • Cross-functional relationships. You have a curiosity as to how things work and which individuals you can support and thus that can support you. You ask questions and challenge the status quo if you’ve experienced a better solution.

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

This role is an existing vacancy

#LI-JS1 #LI-Remote #DACH


What We Have to Offer:

Compensation

We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:

  • Germany: €58,800.00 to €120,500.00

  • United States: $91,000.00 to $181,700.00

  • United Kingdom: £57,200.00 to £116,400.00

  • Singapore: S$113,100.00 to S$209,900.00

If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

Benefits & Perks

data.title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
data.description:
Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)

Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director

About Everfield

Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.

We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.

The Opportunity

The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.

This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.

Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.

How the Role Operates

• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.

• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.

• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.

• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.

What You Will Do

Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration

• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.

• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.

• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.

• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.

• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.

• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.

• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.

Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity

• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.

• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.

• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.

• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.

Revenue Standards & Definitions

• Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.

• Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.

• Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.

Commercial Governance

• Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.

• Support commission structure alignment with business goals.

• Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.

Commercial Diagnostics

• Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.

• Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.

data.title: Member of Technical Staff - Safety
data.description:
About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We're creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why this role

FLUX models ship as open weights, which gives anyone full access to the model. Our safety efforts focus on suppressing harmful behaviors and mitigating the risk of misuse, so safety has to be built into the models themselves, not bolted on afterwards.

As a Member of Technical Staff on our safety research team, you'll research and ship methods that make FLUX models safe by design: from what goes into the training data to how the models are mid- and post-trained, across images, video and the text that conditions them. This is a role with real ownership: you won't just do research on model safety, you'll shape it. The methods you build ship in FLUX models with over 75 million downloads on Hugging Face and in production at some of the largest platforms in the world.

What you'll work on

  • Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure.

  • Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs.

  • Make safety hold up for open-weight releases, including robustness to adversarial prompts and to downstream fine-tuning.

  • Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models.

  • Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance.

  • Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense.

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks.

  • Proven experience in at least one of:

    • Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more.

    • Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models.

  • Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts.

  • Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab.

  • Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale.

  • Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result.

  • Experience running multi-agent workflows: you know which tasks to hand off and which to keep yourself, and you use the speed-up to raise the quality bar, not lower it.

We'd be especially excited if you:

  • Know how to keep safety intact after release, when others fine-tune open weights.

  • Have tackled safety for video generation, where harm can emerge across frames rather than in any single frame.

  • Bring experience with audio safety, especially for jointly generated audio and video, where each modality can amplify harm in the other.

  • Have unlearned concepts from text encoders or built safety-tuned encoders (e.g. Safe-CLIP-style approaches).

  • Have worked on text safety: LLM safety tuning, prompt and jailbreak defenses, or text safety classifiers, ideally across languages.

  • Have applied latent-space safety methods, such as activation steering or safe guidance.

  • Have built VLM-based safety judges or guard models for filtering or evaluation.

How we work together

We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You'll join us in Freiburg at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all. We'll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

  • Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

  • Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

  • Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you.

Compensation

EUR 160K-220K + equity, depending on profile

data.title: Robotics Application Engineer
data.description:
At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.

Robotics Application Engineer – Rhoda AI GmbH (Germany)

About Rhoda AI GmbH
Rhoda AI GmbH is Rhoda AI's first international entity, established to own strategic partner relationships across Europe and drive deployment of Robotics as a Service (RaaS). It's a small, high-ownership team: you'll work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one, with a direct line to our engineering organization in Silicon Valley.

About the Application Engineering Team
Application Engineering is where Rhoda's AI meets the real world. We work directly with customers and strategic partners to understand their operational problems, determine where our platform can deliver value, and lead the application of Rhoda's AI model end to end — from model post-training and data collection, to robot tooling and work-cell design, to production deployments on the customer's floor. The team sits at the intersection of engineering, product, deployment operations, and business, with members in the US and Germany. Application Engineering is organized into three complementary roles — Application Engineers, Solution Engineers, and Technical Program Managers.

The Role
As a Robotics Application Engineer, you are a core member of Rhoda AI's European team and the hands-on technical lead in the early stages of a partner engagement — Scoping, Proof of Principle (POP), and Proof of Concept (POC) — through to RaaS deployment. You'll determine whether a use case is feasible, design and prototype the end effectors and task tooling a robot needs to do the job, write the data collection procedures that feed our models, and post-train Rhoda's AI model to perform the task. You'll spend real time on partner sites across Europe standing up POCs and showing what our platform can do.

You'll also serve as a key technical bridge between our European partners and Rhoda HQ Engineering, owning the feedback loop that turns field findings into product improvements.

What You'll Do

  • Scope new partner use cases alongside the commercial team: ask the right questions, assess technical feasibility, and make go/no-go recommendations.

  • Design, prototype, and iterate on end effectors and task-specific tooling for real-world manipulation tasks.

  • Author and refine data collection SOPs, and work with teleoperation and ML ops teams to gather high-quality training data.

  • Post-train and evaluate Rhoda's AI model on partner tasks, driving performance toward POC success criteria.

  • Lead on-site POP/POC setup and execution, including model training, daily reporting, validation, and direct partner interaction, and author the final technical report.

  • Partner with Solution Engineers on task engineering and solution design input as engagements move toward production.

  • Review proposals and provide technical feedback ahead of purchase orders.

  • Support model training through Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), deployment, and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT).

  • Lead root cause analysis for issues surfaced during deployments, troubleshooting across hardware, firmware, and software until the real cause is found.

  • Share field learnings with product and engineering in Silicon Valley, translating partner-reported issues into prioritized, actionable input for the roadmap.

  • Present clear, non-technical summaries of technical outcomes to partner leadership, and work with the commercial team to tie them to commercial milestones.

What You'll Bring

  • BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 3–8 years of hands-on experience in robotics, automation, systems integration, or applied engineering in an industrial setting, including real-world deployments or field installations.

  • Strong mechanical design skills, including CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion) and rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining, off-the-shelf components).

  • Working knowledge of machine learning workflows — data collection, training, and evaluation — and comfort working in Python.

  • Experience with robot arms, grippers, and sensors (cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR, IMUs) in real environments, including integration and calibration.

  • Proven track record conducting root cause analysis on complex systems spanning hardware, firmware, and software.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

  • Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to partners, executives, and internal teams. Fluent English required; German at working level minimum.

  • Willingness to travel approximately 40% across Europe, including extended on-site POC periods, with occasional travel to the US.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with imitation learning, VLA models, world models, or robot foundation models.

  • Background in factory automation, material handling, or logistics.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role (application, field, FDE, or sales engineering) at a robotics OEM, system integrator, or corporate automation department.

  • Familiarity with teleoperation systems or remote robot management workflows.

  • Experience with ROS/ROS2, embedded Linux, or C/Rust for onboard software.

Why Rhoda AI GmbH

  • Work on real customer problems, not lab demos: our robots are ready for field deployment directly after a successful POC.

  • Direct line to HQ Engineering — your field intelligence shapes the product roadmap.

  • Small, high-ownership team where you work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one.

data.title: AI Fabric Architect
data.description:
fal is the generative media ecosystem powering the next generation of AI products. We build the infrastructure, tools, and model access that teams need to move from idea to production, and do it at scale without compromise. For developers and enterprises, fal is the foundation that makes generative media not just possible, but practical: a unified platform where high-performance inference, orchestration, and observability come together to unlock new categories of AI-native products.

As generative media reshapes industries across a market projected to grow by hundreds of billions over the next decade, fal is becoming the ecosystem that ambitious teams build on.

About this role

You are the architect of the network that our GPU clusters run on. You own the fabric end to end, from the NIC in each GPU server through the spine and leaf across the AI fabric, and you know that in AI infrastructure the network is core to the machine. As fal brings its own GPU capacity online across multiple sites, you will define the fabric architecture every site is built from, and then personally make sure it gets built and performs. This is not an architecture-only role. We are a small team moving fast, and the right person is as comfortable writing a port map, tracing a bad optic, or tuning congestion control on the data center floor as they are setting technical direction.

What you will do:

  • Own the fabric architecture for every site: GPU backend fabric (InfiniBand and/or RoCEv2), and GPU frontend Fabric

  • Choose topologies and make the key calls: rail-optimized vs. other designs, InfiniBand vs. Ethernet, oversubscription ratios, and how the fabric scales from one pod to many

  • Turn the architecture into a repeatable network blueprint: cabling plans, port maps, fabric addressing and routing design, and a fabric bill of materials (switches, NICs, optics, cables)

  • Get hands-on with bring-up at each site: be on the floor for the first racks, validate cabling and firmware, configure the fabric manager and switches, and run performance acceptance (NCCL tests, burn-in) before capacity goes live

  • Tune for real workload performance: congestion control, PFC/ECN, adaptive routing, and NCCL settings for both inference and training traffic

  • Debug fabric problems wherever they show up, from a flapping link to a job that’s mysteriously slow

  • Evaluate and select AI Fabric vendors and hardware, and push back with data when something doesn’t meet spec

  • Collaborate across automation and software to help build network monitoring, telemetry, and automation that let a small team run a large fleet, and be the top escalation point for AI Fabric incidents

  • Document as you go so each new site is faster than the last, and help hire and mentor the network engineers who join after you

Qualifications:

  • 7+ years in data center or HPC networking, including direct responsibility for production GPU cluster fabrics

  • A track record of taking GPU fabrics from empty racks to production, with your own hands on the work, not only through vendors or integrators

  • Deep expertise in InfiniBand (NDR/XDR, UFM, subnet management) and/or RoCEv2 lossless Ethernet

  • Strong command of rail-optimized and Clos/fat-tree designs, BGP/ECMP, and EVPN/VXLAN

  • A clear understanding of how fabric design and tuning affect collective communication and real workload performance

  • Comfortable automating with Python, Ansible, or similar

  • Strong Linux skills and the ability to debug across the boundary between host, NIC, and fabric

  • Sound judgment on tradeoffs between cost, performance, reliability, and time to deploy

  • NVIDIA Quantum/Spectrum-X, ConnectX-7/8, BlueField-3 SuperNICs, and/or Broadcom Tomahawk 5-class Ethernet

  • 400G/800G OSFP optics, AOC/DAC, MPO trunking

Nice to have:

  • Experience at a neocloud, hyperscaler AI infrastructure team, NVIDIA networking, or an AI factory integrator

  • Experience with NVLink / NVL72-class rack-scale systems and how they change scale-out fabric design

  • Experience with GPUDirect RDMA and GPUDirect Storage networks

  • Experience building out multiple sites in parallel or on aggressive timelines

  • Willingness to travel frequently to data center sites, especially during build-outs

data.title: Speditionskaufmann/-frau
data.description:
Als Speditionskaufmann/-frau übernimmst du die Organisation und Abwicklung nationaler und internationaler Transporte und sorgst dafür, dass Sendungen termingerecht, korrekt dokumentiert und wirtschaftlich beim Ziel ankommen. Du bist die zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Kund:innen, Lieferanten und Spediteuren, kalkulierst Transportkosten und behältst Liefertermine sowie Zollformalitäten jederzeit im Blick. In dieser Rolle für den deutschen Markt gestaltest du aktiv reibungslose Logistikprozesse und trägst direkt zur Zuverlässigkeit unserer Lieferkette bei.

PERGOLUX entwirft, produziert und verkauft hochwertige, skandinavisch inspirierte Produkte für das Leben im Freien, darunter Pergolen und Gartenmöbel. Mit rund 300 Mitarbeiter:innen, einem Umsatz im neunstelligen Bereich und einer Präsenz in acht Märkten sind wir ein stetig wachsendes Premium-E-Commerce-Unternehmen mit einem engagierten, internationalen Team.

Deine Aufgaben

- Organisation und Abwicklung von nationalen und internationalen Transporten sowie Koordination mit Kund:innen, Lieferanten und Spediteuren

- Erstellung von Fracht- und Zolldokumenten

- Kalkulation von Transportkosten und Überwachung von Lieferterminen

- Bearbeitung von Reklamationen und Schadensfällen

- Dokumentation, Archivierung von Transportunterlagen sowie administrative Tätigkeiten im Bereich Logistik

Dein Profil

- Deutschkenntnisse auf C2-Niveau und Englischkenntnisse auf C1-Niveau

- 2–3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Bereich Spedition oder Logistik

- Starke organisatorische und kommunikative Fähigkeiten

- Sicherer Umgang mit MS Office und idealerweise Erfahrung mit Logistiksoftware

- Teamorientierte, lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise und Eigeninitiative, auch in stressigen Situationen

💼 Vergütung — Attraktives Gehalt, das deine Expertise widerspiegelt und Ergebnisse belohnt · Betriebliche Altersvorsorge · Bezahlte, gedeckelte Überstunden ohne endlose unbezahlte Crunch-Phasen

🚀 Wachstum und Karriereentwicklung — Vom Start an übernimmst du echte Verantwortung mit direktem Einfluss auf zentrale Geschäftsergebnisse, arbeitest in einem internationalen, kooperativen Team mit Kolleg:innen in ganz Europa und kannst mit dem Wachstum von PERGOLUX in weiterführende Rollen hineinwachsen.

⏰ Urlaub und Flexibilität — Bis zu 30 Urlaubstage, beginnend mit 27 · Eine Woche Remote-Workation pro Jahr in der EU/UK

🌟 Benefits und Lifestyle

- Jobrad / Bike-Leasing-Programm für nachhaltiges und gesundes Pendeln

- Moderne Ausstattung und Laptops (Apple oder Windows)

- Mitarbeiter:innenrabatte auf PERGOLUX-Produkte

- Teamkultur mit regelmäßigen Team-Events (Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier, After-Work-Treffen) und Retreats

📍 Bürostandort – Seelbüde 13, 36110 Schlitz, gut mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln erreichbar

So bewirbst du dich

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung inklusive Lebenslauf. Bewirb dich direkt über unsere [Career Page](https://pergolux.careers/) und erfahre mehr über unsere Kultur auf [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pergolux/posts/?feedView=all).

data.title: Sales Excellence Manager
data.description:
As a Sales Excellence Manager (m/w/d), you will find where our sales funnel leaks and where we engage customers too slowly, then work with the sales teams until it is fixed across our global markets. You will own revenue per worked hour as our core productivity KPI, run capacity planning and bonus governance, and set the build priorities that turn your findings into tools. Analysis is your starting point, not your deliverable: you are measured on whether conversion, speed to lead and productivity actually move in each market.

PERGOLUX designs and sells premium, Scandinavian-inspired outdoor living products, from aluminium pergolas to garden furniture, directly to consumers. We need someone who has already managed product designers and can do it well from day one.

n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems your team tackles are complex. Design decisions have to account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes ripple across the whole platform. You'll need enough craft depth to recognise excellent work, challenge it constructively, and help designers get better. The team needs a manager whose design judgment they trust.

You'll manage a team spanning product designers, design engineers and user researchers at a range of seniority levels, working across our product areas. You'll work alongside our other design manager. You'll report to our VP of Product until our Head of Design joins the team. That search is running now.

More than 80% of workflows built on n8n involve AI agents, and we're widening from a developer audience to a broader set of builders. That shift is the central design problem here, and your team is at the centre of it.

🎯 Your main goal is to build a Product Design team that consistently produces excellent work and shapes how n8n's product evolves. Here's what that involves:


Lead and develop the team

  • Run regular, high-quality 1:1s and coach designers, design engineers and researchers across different levels.

  • Own performance management: evidence-based reviews, honest feedback, and real support for anyone who isn't where they need to be.

  • Help people understand what's expected at their level and what growth looks like, evolving our progression framework for Product Design.

  • Hire excellent designers as the team grows, and broaden the range of backgrounds and perspectives on the team.

Raise the design bar

  • Set and hold a high standard across problem framing, user understanding, interaction design, information architecture and visual craft.

  • Facilitate design critiques and reviews that measurably improve the work, and help designers think beyond the feature in front of them.

  • Develop designers' judgment and autonomy rather than becoming the final approval layer for every decision.

Own the whole product experience

  • Keep a holistic view across features and product areas, identifying inconsistencies, recurring UX problems, and opportunities for more coherent patterns.

  • Work with the team to address fragmentation systematically rather than feature by feature.

Make design a real partner

  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering leadership so design contributes early to problem definition and product direction, not late to execution.

  • Help designers influence product decisions through strong reasoning rather than positional authority.

  • Improve how the team works across critique, collaboration, decision-making and knowledge sharing, introducing structure where it helps the team scale and resisting process that slows things down.

How much of this is hands-on?

Worth being direct, because it's the question every good candidate asks. This is a management role: developing designers, raising the bar, and making design count in product decisions is the job, and that's where your time goes.

You'll stay close to the craft in critiques, in reviews and in the detail of the work, and you'll occasionally pick up design work yourself. When that happens it sits outside the squads and varies with the period: an exploratory concept, a gap during someone's leave, a problem that needs a first pass. It is not a 50/50 split, and if what you want is to keep a squad's worth of delivery alongside managing the team, this isn't the role.

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

  • 👥 Proven design management: You've managed product designers in a product-led technology company for 3+ years, with a team of five or more. This is not a first management role.

  • 🧭 Running a team well: You've run effective 1:1s, evidence-based performance reviews and difficult feedback conversations, including with people who weren't performing. You've built or improved a career progression framework for designers, and you're comfortable with the administrative side of managing a team rather than treating it as overhead.

  • 📈 Growing people: You coach and mentor, you run critique that changes the work, and you can point to specific designers who got measurably better or grew in scope while reporting to you.

  • 🎨 Design taste and judgment: Your own craft is strong enough that designers trust your read on quality, you can articulate what separates adequate design from excellent design, and you'll step into the work directly when the situation calls for it.

  • 🎯 Hiring: You've hired designers consistently well, you know where good design talent is and how to attract it, and you can tell the difference quickly.

  • 🤖 AI fluency: You use AI tools hands-on in your own work and in how your team designs, and you have an informed view on designing AI-enabled products. AI agents are the product here, so this one is not optional.

Nice-to-haves

  • 🛠️ Technical products: You've managed design teams in B2B SaaS, developer tools, workflow automation or similarly technical products.

  • 🧠 Technical mindset: You don't need to write code, but genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath (APIs, webhooks, data structures, how workflows actually execute) earns you credibility with engineers here.

  • 👩‍💻 Designing for developers: You've designed products for developers, technical operators or other sophisticated users.

  • 🔭 Systems view: You can step back from individual projects to spot patterns and UX problems across a broader product experience.

  • 🤝 Influence without authority: You bring Product and Engineering peers with you through reasoning rather than positional authority.

  • 📊 Scaling teams: You've grown a design team through a period of rapid company growth.

  • 🌍 Distributed teams: You've managed designers in remote-first or highly distributed organisations.

  • 🔓 Open source: You've worked on open-source or community-driven products.

  • 🌱 Inclusive hiring: You've meaningfully broadened the diversity of a design team through how you hire.

Our hiring process

We'll tell you the whole shape of it upfront, and there's very little homework.

  1. Screening call with our recruiter. 45 minutes, no prep.

  2. Leading designers with the hiring manager, 75 minutes. You'll present for 20 minutes on a team you built, grew or turned around. Reuse existing material; it shouldn't take more than two or three hours. We don't need case studies of your own design work.

  3. Live critique and coaching, 60 minutes. We'll send you a real piece of n8n design work 24 hours ahead. You'll critique it, then have a coaching conversation with the designer who made it. No preparation beyond reading it and trying the product.

  4. Conversation with our VP of Product, and a culture call with Jan, our CEO. 45 minutes each, same day where we can.

  5. Meet two or three of the designers you'd be managing. Not scored; it's for you as much as for us.

We'll also ask for two references, one of them a former direct report. A portfolio is welcome if you have one, though we know not every design manager keeps theirs current.

Why join us?

At n8n, your work won't disappear into a slide deck. You'll lead design for a product that hundreds of thousands of builders use to automate real work, sitting right where developer tools, AI agents and no-code interaction models meet. The design problems are genuinely hard and largely unsolved.

You're inheriting an established team with strong designers, not building from zero, and there's real room to shape how the team coaches, critiques, grows and works with Product and Engineering, rather than inheriting a rigid design organisation. You'll stay close enough to the craft to influence quality directly, while your main job is making the designers around you better.

You'll join a fast-growing, Europe remote-first company where autonomy, experimentation, and craft matter, at the point where n8n is scaling from a beloved open-source project into a major B2B platform. Design's contribution to product thinking is established here, and has a long way still to run.

Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on?

Apply now and help us build the future of automation.

Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:

  • Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

  • Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

  • Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register.

We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

n8n sits at one of the most interesting UX problems in software right now: more than 80% of workflows built on n8n today involve AI agents, and the platform is in the middle of a deliberate expansion from deeply technical developers toward a broader set of builders. That tension, keeping power users happy while dramatically lowering the floor, is the central design challenge.

This is a foundational hire with a real mandate and direct exec partnership.

What you'll do

Own the quality bar

  • Set a clear, consistent quality bar that the team can orient around and build toward, so great work becomes the natural output of how we design together.

  • Build review processes and critique rituals that give the team a shared language for quality and the confidence to make strong craft decisions together.

  • Evolve the design system and QA practices so the bar rises as the team grows.

  • Dig into one of the most genuinely interesting UX challenges in the space: n8n has historically had a steep learning curve for new users. Your job is to lower that floor without losing the power that experienced builders love.

Drive design's strategic influence

  • Shape product strategy, not just respond to it. Bring design thinking into roadmap conversations and help surface user problems before they become someone else's brief.

  • Help lead n8n's expansion toward a broader, less technical audience, a deliberate and exciting strategic shift that design should be leading.

  • Build the kind of relationships with Product, Engineering, and leadership where design is a genuine thought partner at every stage.

Build and grow the team

  • Lead a team of around 14 designers today: 2 Design Leads each working with ~6 ICs, plus Design Engineering and UX Research (with more hires ahead).

  • Shape the team structure, career framework, and progression paths so people know where they stand and where they're going.

  • Create a culture of high standards and honest feedback, where people feel supported to do their best work and have a clear sense of what great looks like.

  • Own hiring and headcount planning for the department, and help us grow without losing what makes the team good.

Build research into how we make decisions

  • Establish a pragmatic, continuous research practice from the ground up. We're making our first dedicated UX research hires, so there's real room to shape this.

  • Make customer insight, product data, and community feedback a live input to product decisions, so teams are building from evidence at every step.

  • Connect research to the decisions that matter most: activation, adoption, retention, and helping new users find their way into n8n with confidence.

Help the team work in new ways

  • Champion practical AI adoption inside the design org, from prototyping and research synthesis to design QA and workflow efficiency.

  • Help the team stay curious and current as the tools, patterns, and expectations around AI products continue to evolve fast.

  • Model the kind of working style you want to see: thoughtful, adaptive, and genuinely excited about what's changing.

Requirements

Must-haves

  • 🧭 Product design leadership: You have managed managers, coached senior designers, and built design teams that improve both craft and business outcomes, including making hard performance calls when needed.

  • 🧩 Complex product systems experience: You have led design across complex or developer-facing products where UX quality depends on deep product understanding.

  • 🎨 Craft authority: You are a quality bar, not just someone who appreciates quality. You can identify great work, explain why it's great, and hold the line on standards even when it's uncomfortable.

  • 📣 Strategic influence, not just strategic thinking: You have made design a co-equal in product conversations, not a downstream function. You know how to bring people with you, create debate, and drive decisions.

  • 🔀 Structured problem-solving under ambiguity: You find your way into unclear problems and create a plan. You don't just ask good questions, you answer them. You move forward when there's no map.

  • 🤖 AI-era product judgment: You understand the AI, automation, or adjacent tooling landscape and can turn emerging patterns into usable, trustworthy product experiences.

  • 🔍 Research literacy: You know how to build research into product development so insight becomes part of how teams make decisions, not a separate artifact.

  • 📊 Data-informed decision making: You use product analytics, research, and customer evidence to guide decisions instead of relying on taste or opinion alone.

  • 🧱 Org design and performance management: You can design team structures, define career paths, raise expectations, and handle difficult performance conversations with clarity.

Nice-to-haves

  • 🌱 Open-source or community product experience: You have worked on open-source, fair-code, community-led, or builder-driven products and understand what it means to design for a community that has strong opinions.

  • 💻 Design engineering credibility: You have enough front-end or design engineering fluency to partner deeply on design system adoption and implementation quality.

  • 🌍 Remote-first operating systems: You have built design rituals, critique, QA, and collaboration practices that work across distributed teams and time zones.

  • 🚀 Growth surface experience: You have worked on activation, onboarding, templates, time-to-value, or product-led growth surfaces.

  • ⬆️ Rising Design Manager profile: We are open to someone who has been an exceptional Design Manager and is ready for their first Head-level role, if the fundamentals are exceptional.

  • Develop and enforce security policies in collaboration with internal stakeholders, taking into account industry-specific compliance requirements

  • Perform system hardening and security baseline management for servers, endpoints, and critical infrastructure components.

  • Design, implementation, and operation of firewall infrastructures using Fortinet and Sophos technologies.

data.title: Senior AI Content Producer - Foto, Video, Motion (m/w/d)
data.description:
Bei Rosental Organics bist du kein klassischer Fotograf oder Videograf – du bist der Content Multiplier. Ein Shoot wird bei dir zu 50+ Assets, ein UGC-Clip zu 30 Hook-Variants, ein Produktfoto zu 20 Format-Adaptionen. Der Meta-Algorithmus belohnt Volumen und Diversität, und genau das lieferst du: aus einer Kampagne wird bei dir ein ganzer Wochen-Feed für Paid Social.

  • Du produzierst und multiplizierst Foto-, Video- und Motion-Content für Paid Ads, Social, CRM und E-Commerce, mit klarem Fokus auf Performance und Testing-Volumen.

  • Du drehst und shootest schnell und hands-on mit modernem Setup: UGC, Product, Lifestyle, Studio – End-to-End und ohne Assistenz-Kette.

  • Einen skalierbaren AI-Workflow baust du selbst auf, der Rohmaterial in Dutzende testbare Variants verwandelt: Hook-Iterations, Cutdowns, Format-Adaptions, Kontext-Wechsel, Voiceover-Varianten, Motion-Loops.

  • Du entwickelst High-Performing Creatives für Meta, TikTok und CRM mit Fokus auf Hook Rate, Watchtime, CTR und ROAS.

  • Mindestens 3 neue AI-Tools pro Jahr integrierst du produktiv in unseren Stack (Runway, Nano Banana, Kive, ElevenLabs, Topaz, CapCut AI, Descript – was heute liefert, ersetzt du morgen).

  • Performance-Dashboards liest du selbst, ziehst die Insights und übersetzt sie am gleichen Tag in neue Variants und Hypothesen.


  • Du bringst 3+ Jahre Erfahrung in Content Production für D2C/ E-Commerce, Performance Marketing oder ein hochdynamisches Growth-Umfeld mit, inklusive starker Paid-Social-Cases (Meta, TikTok).

  • Dein Portfolio zeigt echte Performance-Ergebnisse (Hook Rate, Watchtime, CTR, ROAS) und Beispiele, wie du aus einem Asset viele gemacht hast, keine Editorial-Reels, keine Behance-Moodboards.

  • Neue AI-Tools lernst du eigenständig und schnell: Runway, Nano Banana, Kive, ElevenLabs, CapCut AI, Descript und Topaz sind dir vertraut, und den nächsten Tool-Sprung hast du meist schon selbst identifiziert.

  • Du drehst, shootest und schneidest selbst (≥ 85 %): Sony/Canon, Studio-Light und Natural-Light, Premiere Pro, CapCut, Photoshop und Lightroom auf sehr hohem Niveau, mit Meta-Funnel-Logik im Schlaf (Hooks Sek. 1, Pattern Interrupt, Pacing).

  • Aus einem Shot 50 Assets zu machen, klingt für dich nach Chance statt Qualitätsverlust; Premium-Ästhetik ohne Kompromisse ist für dich selbstverständlich, AI-Output darf nie nach AI-Output aussehen.

  • Du liest Zahlen und übersetzt sie direkt in Creative-Entscheidungen, strukturiert, direkt, belastbar. Deutsch mind. C1.

data.description:
About Us

Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity.

Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance.

We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth.

Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures.

 

Position Overview

We’re looking for a Senior Compliance Consultant to help our clients navigate regulatory change, horizon-scan upcoming regulation, and overcome regulatory challenges so they can transform their businesses and meet their strategic growth objectives.

This is a versatile, high-impact role at the intersection of regulation, client advisory, practical delivery and product strategy. Your mission is to deeply understand our clients’ needs and regulatory obligations, and to deliver solutions that help them achieve their compliance and business outcomes. You’ll stay ahead of the risk and compliance landscape, translating regulatory change into clear guidance for our customers and concrete requirements for our Product team.

Whether you’re shaping a client’s regulatory strategy or influencing our product roadmap, you’ll bring deep knowledge and hands-on experience of financial crime compliance, along with strong commercial awareness. Acting as an in-house consultant, you’ll connect long-term regulatory horizons with granular operational realities.

 

As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move comfortably between complex challenges, and have the judgement to turn them into sharp, practical solutions. You’ll also work on long-horizon strategic projects, such as building government relationships and expanding Condukt’s global data footprint, where progress is measured in weeks, not months.

If you thrive in dynamic environments where no two days look the same, enjoy tackling a constant stream of new and complex problems, and want to help shape how financial institutions and fintechs approach compliance, this role is for you.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Act as Condukt’s subject matter expert on KYB/KYC and AML/CFT, giving clients clear, commercially minded advice on their regulatory obligations

  • Lead client engagements end to end, from understanding the business challenge and assessing current controls to designing solutions that combine Condukt’s platform with third-party providers and supporting their implementation

  • Produce high-quality, client-ready deliverables, such as gap analyses, risk assessments, onboarding and monitoring frameworks, policies and decision papers

  • Run workshops with client stakeholders, from compliance teams to the C-suite, turning discussion into practical next steps

  • Horizon-scan regulation across the UK, Europe and beyond, and brief clients on what’s coming and what it means for them, directly or alongside our commercial team

  • Advise clients on their compliance stack, testing and benchmarking providers through structured, RFP-style evaluations

  • Build and maintain relationships with regulators, government bodies and company registers to secure access to data, expand Condukt’s global footprint and represent Condukt in industry forums

  • Shape Condukt’s advisory proposition, identifying emerging client needs and opportunities to bring new capabilities to existing clients alongside our commercial team

  • Partner with Product to translate regulatory and client needs into the signals, data and capabilities we build

  • Contribute to business development and thought leadership with a clear, well-argued point of view on regulation, through proposals, client pitches, whitepapers, briefings, webinars and industry events

 

What you bring:

  • 4+ years’ experience in financial crime compliance, gained in a consultancy, a regulator or a regulated financial services firm

  • Deep domain expertise in risk and compliance, ideally across KYB/KYC, AML/CFT or business onboarding in financial services

  • A track record of advising financial institutions and fintechs on risk, compliance or regulatory matters, with a toolkit of structured frameworks you can adapt to a fast-growing company

  • Experience leading client engagements and producing polished, client-ready deliverables

  • Experience advising on vendor assessment and selection, including running or contributing to RFP processes

  • Proven ability to build trusted relationships with C-suite stakeholders, regulators and government agencies

  • Strong commercial awareness: you can turn regulatory requirements into solutions clients see real value in

  • A legal background, or solid working knowledge of financial regulation and how legislation translates into operational requirements

  • Sound judgement and tact in sensitive situations: you know what to communicate, to whom and when

  • The analytical rigour to dig into complex legislation and question established interpretations

  • A self-starter mindset that thrives in fast-moving, high-ownership environments

Bonus:

  • Experience in government relations or regulatory affairs

  • Prior experience in fintech, banking, payments or compliance infrastructure

  • Early-stage startup experience

  • Second language proficiency (German, French, and Dutch, especially valued)

 

Our offer:

  • Tackle meaningful problems with real-world impact

  • Competitive salary and equity package

  • Flat hierarchy with direct access to the founders

  • Top-of-the-line equipment

  • Private health insurance, plus sick and compassionate leave as needed

data.description:
About 1st Formations

At 1st Formations, we empower entrepreneurs to start, run, and grow their businesses with confidence.

Running a business shouldn't be slowed down by company formation, statutory compliance, accounting, or payroll. From day one, these essentials should be seamless, reliable, and intelligently handled — freeing founders to focus on building and scaling.

We're a leading UK provider of company formation and compliance services, building a modern, fully integrated technology platform that supports founders at every stage of their journey. Our platform brings together formation, compliance, accounting, payroll, and ongoing business support in one cohesive experience.

No stitched-together services. No legacy workflows disguised as software. Just a single, scalable platform built for ambitious founders who want to move fast, stay compliant, and grow with confidence.

Why Join Us Now?

You'll be joining a business with strong momentum, clear direction, and real opportunity for progression.

  • £18m annual revenue, including £9m ARR

  • Over 1 million companies formed

  • Certified B Corp and Carbon Neutral Business

  • Forecast to grow 5x–10x over the next three years

The Role

We're looking for a commercially minded, customer-focused Customer Retention Executive to protect and grow our client base, primarily across our company formations and compliance services, while also supporting retention efforts for our formations business. You'll own the retention experience - proactively engaging with customers, understanding their needs, and stepping in early when accounts show signs of risk. This is a relationship-driven role at its core: you'll balance customer advocacy with commercial objectives, turning at-risk accounts into loyal, long-term clients.

Key Responsibilities

  • Proactively engage with existing customers to understand their needs, address concerns, and identify opportunities to retain and grow accounts through tailored solutions and timely interventions

  • Take ownership of at-risk customers, managing objections and resolving service issues to rebuild confidence and prevent churn

  • Act as a trusted point of contact for small business clients, company directors, and accountancy professionals, balancing customer advocacy with commercial objectives

  • Collaborate closely with internal teams to deliver outcomes that reinforce customer confidence and loyalty

  • Analyse customer behaviour and monitor retention and usage metrics across our formations, compliance, and accounting platforms to identify at-risk accounts early

  • Continuously refine engagement strategies based on data to improve customer lifetime value

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of customer interactions, risk flags, and outcomes in internal systems

  • Support retention activity for our formations and compliance clients

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience in a customer retention, account management, or client relationship role, ideally within company formations, compliance, or professional/financial services (accountancy sector or technology platform experience is a plus)

  • Commercially minded and customer-focused, with a strong ability to build lasting client relationships and reduce churn in a fast-paced environment

  • Confident managing objections and resolving service issues while keeping the client's confidence intact

  • Good understanding of company formation and compliance workflows, and the challenges small business owners face

  • Data-driven and resilient: comfortable analysing customer behaviour and retention/usage metrics to inform your approach

  • Motivated by results, with a track record of improving customer lifetime value and delivering a consistent, positive customer experience

  • A strong collaborator, able to work closely with internal teams to escalate and resolve issues

What We Offer

  • £30,000–£35,000 salary and comprehensive benefits package

data.title: DevEx Engineer IV
data.description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role:

Zilch's DevOps team is a small team with a large surface area: four engineers supporting an engineering organisation of over a hundred. The team's mission is to make engineering at Zilch faster, safer, and less painful, by building tooling and automation that lets product teams focus on shipping rather than fighting their environment.

We're looking for a software engineer who cares deeply about developer experience. Someone who's spent enough time building products to know where the friction is (slow feedback loops, flaky pipelines, manual toil, poor tooling) and who wants to fix those problems properly. Not with quick patches, but with well-built internal tools that engineers actually want to use.

You'll own problems end-to-end: understanding what's slowing engineers down, deciding what to build, building it, and driving adoption. The role blends product thinking with hands-on engineering; you'll shape what the team works on as much as you'll write the code.

One example of what this team builds: our ephemeral environments platform, which spins up full, sandboxed copies of the Zilch stack on demand for development, debugging, and automated testing. It's integrated into the PR workflow, backed by its own orchestration engine, and has fundamentally changed how engineers work here. You'd be working with and extending capabilities like this.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape how an engineering organisation works; not just keep the lights on.

What you'll do:

  • Identify the biggest sources of developer friction across the organisation and turn them into well-scoped improvements

  • Design and build internal tools, automation, and self-service capabilities that make engineers' lives measurably better

  • Own adoption: build things that solve real problems and communicate them well enough that teams actually use them

  • Work across engineering to understand workflows, pain points, and opportunities; act as an advocate for developer experience in technical decisions

  • Raise the bar within the team: through code quality, design thinking, and setting standards for how the team approaches its work

  • Contribute to the team's support rotation, and use that exposure to inform what the team builds next

What we’re looking for:

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals. You write clean, well-structured code and care about maintainability, testing, and good API design

  • Product-minded. You think about who's using what you build, what problem it solves, and whether people will actually adopt it. You'd rather build the right thing than the most technically interesting thing

  • Empathy for developer experience. You've been the engineer fighting the tooling, and you want to be the one who fixes it

  • Proactive and entrepreneurial. You see gaps and opportunities and move on them without waiting for permission; you make the case for what to build rather than waiting for it to be assigned

  • Technically credible. You can hold your own in architectural discussions with experienced infrastructure engineers

  • Familiarity with infrastructure tooling: Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, cloud platforms (AWS)

  • Organisational awareness. You know how to navigate a medium-to-large engineering org to get things built and adopted; shipping good tooling is as much about communication as it is about code

  • Comfortable representing your team's work and priorities to senior stakeholders

Bonus skills:

  • Experience with GitOps delivery patterns, ideally with ArgoCD

  • Observability platform experience, particularly OpenTelemetry

  • Experience with other parts of our stack: GitHub Actions, Crossplane, Spacelift, Go, Liquibase

About the role.

This is an exciting opportunity to own the overall fraud strategy at a fast-growing fintech, taking leadership of a critical area of risk and a key driver of Zilch’s commercial performance. Fraud is a highly visible and strategically important P&L item, with significant senior scrutiny, and this role will play a central part in shaping how Zilch protects the business while continuing to deliver a great experience for genuine customers.

As Fraud Strategy Manager, you will be responsible for designing and evolving Zilch’s fraud strategy across both application fraud and in-life fraud. You’ll lead the development of strategies that identify, prevent, and respond to fraud risk at scale, ensuring controls are effective, data-driven, and commercially balanced.

The role sits at the intersection of Risk, Fraud Operations, Product, Engineering, Data, and Compliance. You’ll work closely with these teams to turn insight into action, developing measures that protect Zilch from fraud while keeping customer journeys as smooth and proportionate as possible.
